chunks: And he (peace be upon him) said:

There are two kinds of workers in the world. One is a person who works in this world for this world, and his worldly life has occupied him from the hereafter. He fears poverty for those he leaves behind, but feels safe about himself, so he spends his life in the benefit of others. And the other is one who works in this world for what is to come after it, and what is his share of this world comes to him without effort, so he secures both shares together, and becomes the owner of both houses (world and hereafter) entirely, so he becomes prestigious before Allah. If he asks Allah for anything, He does not deny him.
ai.seo_question: What is the difference between working for this world versus working for the hereafter according to Imam Ali?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (peace be upon him) contrasts the 'worker for the world' who exhausts his life serving others to secure his heirs' wealth, with the 'worker for the hereafter' who effortlessly acquires worldly benefits as a byproduct of spiritual devotion. This dichotomy highlights the Shia concept of *al-kasb al-mubham* (ambiguous acquisition), where the righteous attain both worlds (*al-darain*) not by neglecting worldly duties, but by aligning their labor with divine purpose, thereby securing high status (*wajih*) with Allah.

en.sayed-ali-raza: 269. Amīr al-mu’minīn, peace be upon him, said:

There are two kinds of workers in the world. One is a person who works in this world for this world and his work of this world keeps him unmindful of the next world. He is afraid of destitution for those he will leave behind but feels himself safe about it. So, he spends his life after the good of others. The other is one who works in this world for what is to come hereafter, and he secures his share of this world without effort. Thus, he gets both the benefits together and becomes the owner of both the houses together. In this way, he is prestigious before Allāh. If he asks Allāh anything He does not deny him.
